A Proposal for Integrating a Multivariate Density

Source: R/multivariate.R
mv_reference_draw.Rd

Draws from a distribution that dominates the family, together with the log-density of those draws, so that an importance-sampling estimate of \(\int f = 1\) can be formed.

Usage

mv_reference_draw(distrib, theta, n, ...)

Arguments

distrib

An object inheriting from class multivariate_distrib.

theta

A named list or vector of parameters.

n

The number of draws.

...

Passed to methods.

Value

A list with y, a matrix of n draws, and logd, their log-density under the proposal.

Details

The default proposal is a gaussian with the same mean and twice the covariance, which serves any family supported on all of \(\mathbb{R}^p\). The inflation matters: a proposal equal to the distribution itself makes every ratio one and certifies nothing.

A family whose support is a lower-dimensional subset of \(\mathbb{R}^p\), such as a Dirichlet on the simplex, must register its own method, because a proposal spread over the ambient space places no mass at all on the support and the estimate would be zero. The draws and the log-density must be taken with respect to the same dominating measure the family's density is written against.

This is consumed by check_distrib and by nothing else. A discrete family does not need it, its normalization being an exact sum over mv_support.

See also

check_distrib, mv_support

Examples

d <- mvgaussian_distrib(2)
theta <- list(mu1 = 0, mu2 = 0, sigma_log_L1 = 0, sigma_log_L2 = 0, sigma_L2.1 = 0)
set.seed(1)
str(mv_reference_draw(d, theta, 5))
#> List of 2
#>  $ y   : num [1:5, 1:2] -0.886 0.26 -1.182 2.256 0.466 ...
#>   ..- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
#>   .. ..$ : NULL
#>   .. ..$ : chr [1:2] "v1" "v2"
#>  $ logd: num [1:5] -3.06 -2.67 -3.15 -3.97 -2.63
